stories.headline: Cruz says Vance is ‘feeling insecure’ after the VP called a 2028 run obvious
stories.summary: Sen. Ted Cruz told Politico on Saturday that Vice President JD Vance is “feeling insecure” after Vance said in an NBC interview that it was “really obvious” Cruz is already running for president in 2028. Cruz said people “engage in political bomb-throwing when they’re feeling insecure” and that he will stay focused on helping Republicans win the midterms in the next 30 days. Vance said he is not running and is trying to elect Republicans. Cruz, who sought the nomination in 2016, has said he will “certainly be part of the discussion.”

stories.headline: Coast Guard won’t say if the Nantucket jet search has become a recovery
stories.summary: At a Sunday news conference, Coast Guard Rear Adm. Matt Lake said crews, Massachusetts authorities, and the New York National Guard have searched about 2,840 square miles over more than 53 hours for six people aboard a medical jet that vanished Saturday off Nantucket. He would not say whether the mission has shifted from rescue to recovery, and he said there is no sign a flight recorder has been found in the extensive debris field about 20 miles offshore. The Latitude Air Ambulance Gulfstream was flying from Bermuda to Boston with four Canadians and two Bermudians, a patient and the patient’s son. Controllers lost contact as the jet dropped from 24,000 feet to 11,000 feet. Lake said crews hope to search the seabed with sonar.

stories.headline: Rahm Emanuel tells Democrats not to impeach Trump if they take the House
stories.summary: On NBC’s Meet the Press Sunday, former Chicago mayor and Obama chief of staff Rahm Emanuel told Democrats not to impeach President Trump if they win the House. He said an impeachment “is not going anywhere” and would turn into “a food fight” that proves Washington is “Disneyland on the Potomac.” He urged the party to deliver an ethics package instead of another round of investigations that go nowhere. Democrats currently hold a significant polling edge heading into the midterms.

stories.headline: Oz calls Obamacare ‘phantom accounts’ fraud and wants broker calls recorded
stories.summary: CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz is pressing health insurers to work only with brokers who record their calls with Obamacare applicants, widening the Trump administration’s crackdown on unauthorized enrollments. He told Fox News Digital the accounts are “phantom accounts” with “no human beings” behind them: no claims filed, no answers to agency questions, and no Social Security number to check whether someone even qualifies. Vice President JD Vance said Tuesday the anti-fraud task force will remove 750,000 fraudulent Obamacare recipients, a step the administration says will save taxpayers $2.2 billion.

stories.headline: Banks says Democrats will block voter ID just to deny Trump a win
stories.summary: Senate Democrats’ refusal to pass a federal voter-ID law is giving Republicans a midterm argument on a practice that is already common in the states and popular with voters in both parties. Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana told Fox News Digital that Democrats will vote no “because they don’t want to give the president a win,” even if it means blocking a bill that also bans congressional insider trading. The latest package follows months of Democratic opposition to the SAVE America Act, a Trump priority that Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has kept out of funding deals.

stories.headline: Trump calls Jack Smith a ‘crooked prosecutor’ over a No Kings festival shirt
stories.summary: President Trump on Sunday called former special counsel Jack Smith a “Crooked Prosecutor” after Smith was seen at Tom Morello’s Power to the People Fest in Maryland wearing a “No Kings” shirt. Trump posted the line on Truth Social alongside a Just the News report on Saturday’s festival, where Bruce Springsteen performed his anti-ICE song “Streets of Minneapolis.” Morello, who organized the show, closed by telling the crowd he hoped they had been “energized, radicalized, revolutionized” and “wound up.”

stories.headline: Angela Paxton says she will vote the GOP ticket without naming Ken Paxton
stories.summary: Texas state Sen. Angela Paxton, who filed for divorce from Senate candidate Ken Paxton last year on “biblical grounds,” says in a new ad that she will vote the Republican ticket on Nov. 3. She never says her estranged husband’s name. “In a general election, it’s not as much about the individual players on the team; it’s about getting the whole team across the finish line,” she says, framing the choice as holding every Republican seat or handing Texas “to the other team.” Ken Paxton faces Democrat James Talarico in a tight race.

stories.headline: Trump posts photos of a ‘crumbling’ Kennedy Center and blames a judge for the delay
stories.summary: President Trump on Sunday posted photos of backstage areas of the Kennedy Center and wrote that the building “is crumbling, and a great danger to anyone who walks inside.” He said it “has been this way for years” and blamed a “Radical Left Judge, with his Trump Hating lawyer wife,” for blocking repairs he says require a temporary closure. Trump, the center’s current chair, has argued the work cannot wait after a piece of the ceiling fell. Critics have said the center should stay open.

stories.headline: Bartender charged after a birthday trip ends in a fatal push down bar stairs
stories.summary: Mary Lopez Hunt, 68, is charged with voluntary manslaughter and aggravated assault after prosecutors say she shoved Joyce Tomlinson, 62, of Minnesota, down the stairs at Coot’s Bar & Grill on Edisto Island, South Carolina. Tomlinson’s childhood friend Ruth Peterson told Fox News Digital she had stepped out to get the car around 11 p.m. on Oct. 3, 2025, while Tomlinson settled the tab on a birthday trip. Peterson said she looked up, saw a brief exchange, and watched Hunt run at Tomlinson and push her with both hands. Peterson spoke to Fox two days before the one-year mark of the death.

stories.headline: Retired pilot who carried Clinton’s nuclear football warns of airline terror cells
stories.summary: Retired Air Force Lt. Col. Buzz Patterson, who carried the nuclear football for President Clinton and later flew for Delta, told Fox News Digital that terror cells inside foreign airlines are “certainly a possibility” after a FlyDubai copilot allegedly attacked the captain of an Israel-bound flight with the cockpit crash ax. Patterson said most vetting still depends on pilots self-reporting, and he wants the Justice Department to look hard at who is in the cockpit. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu told Fox & Friends the copilot appeared to have had “Islamist radical indoctrination.” The Boeing 737, with 174 passengers and eight crew, diverted to Tabuk, Saudi Arabia.

stories.headline: A driverless Cybercab pulls into a Supercharger while one worker plugs in ten cars
stories.summary: A 57-second clip posted Oct. 2 by X user Abhimanyu Yadav shows what he describes as an empty Cybercab arriving at a public Supercharger at night beside nine Model Ys, while one person walks the row and plugs each vehicle in. The post has drawn more than 162,000 views. TeslaNorth notes that “unsupervised,” “public supercharger,” and “Tesla employee” are the poster’s labels and have not been independently verified. Tesla already runs dedicated Robotaxi chargers and recently extended Austin Cybercab service to 11 p.m., while NHTSA is still examining the company’s certification of nearly 1,000 Cybercabs.

stories.headline: Musk says SpaceXAI will be renamed SpaceXSI as he drops the word AI
stories.summary: Elon Musk posted overnight that there should be “No more AI,” that “SI” is better, and that “SpaceX is a super intelligence company.” When a user suggested renaming SpaceXAI to SpaceXSI, Musk replied, “Yes, we will make that change.” It would be the second name for the business in under a year: SpaceX absorbed xAI in an all-stock deal in February, then adopted the SpaceXAI name in July. Musk did not say when the switch takes effect, whether it is a legal rename, or whether the @SpaceXAI handle will change. No company announcement had followed as of Sunday morning.

stories.headline: Gurman: the next MacBook Pro with OLED will be significantly lighter
stories.summary: Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports that Apple’s redesigned MacBook Pro, expected by the end of November, will be significantly lighter after the company miniaturized parts and rearranged the interior. Today’s 16-inch MacBook Pro weighs as much as 4.8 pounds, against 3.3 pounds for the 15-inch MacBook Air, so a real cut would be obvious in a bag. Gurman did not give a new weight. The machines are still expected to ship with M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, skipping the high end of the M6 family, plus OLED, touch, and a Dynamic Island, with macOS changes in Golden Gate and 27.2 to support them.

stories.headline: Geezer Butler joins Jack Black’s Sabbath cover band for ‘War Pigs’
stories.summary: Black Sabbath bassist Geezer Butler walked on with Jack Black’s tribute act Jack Sabbath on Saturday night at Tom Morello’s Power to the People festival in Columbia, Maryland, and played “War Pigs.” Black’s band, with Morello’s son Roman on guitar, Anthrax guitarist Scott Ian’s son Revel on bass, drummer Yoyoka Soma, and keyboardist Hugo Weiss, opened with Ozzy Osbourne’s “Mr. Crowley” and Sabbath’s “The Wizard” before Butler came up. Black has long tied himself to that catalog, from a Tenacious D song named for Ronnie James Dio to his speech when Ozzy entered the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.

stories.headline: Hassett tells Kudlow it’s time for Powell to leave the Fed board
stories.summary: National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett told Larry Kudlow on Sunday Morning Futures that former Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell should leave the Fed board now that his chairmanship is over. Hassett called the extended stay “completely unprecedented” and said Powell should “move on” and “respect the independence of the Fed” rather than keep a visible partisan split inside the central bank. He argued an independent Fed is what the economy needs, and that Powell’s lingering role is getting in the way of that.
